title: Dynamics: Forces, Motion and Terminal Velocity
subject: Physics

questions.question: Which property of a body is a measure of its resistance to change in motion?
questions.explanation: Mass is the measure of a body's resistance to change in motion. The greater the mass, the harder it is to change its state of rest or motion.

questions.question: A skydiver falls at terminal velocity. What is the relationship between air resistance and weight?
options: Air resistance is less than weight
Air resistance is equal to weight
Air resistance is greater than weight
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, acceleration is zero. This means forces are balanced. Therefore, upward air resistance equals downward weight (Syllabus 3m).

questions.question: A resultant force of 20 N acts on a mass of 4 kg. What is the acceleration produced?
questions.explanation: Using Newton's Second Law: F = ma. So a = F/m = 20 N ÷ 4 kg = 5 m/s². An unbalanced force causes acceleration.

questions.question: Which statement about action-reaction pairs is CORRECT?
options: They act on the same body
They are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
They cancel each other out completely
The action force occurs before the reaction force
questions.explanation: Newton's Third Law states action and reaction forces are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, and act on different bodies (Syllabus 3g).

questions.question: A box is pushed with a force of 50 N. The frictional force opposing the motion is 10 N. If the mass of the box is 5 kg, what is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Resultant (unbalanced) force F = Push - Friction = 50 N - 10 N = 40 N. Using F = ma: 40 N = 5 kg × a. So a = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 m/s² (Syllabus 3j).

questions.question: How does the acceleration of a falling object change as it approaches terminal velocity?
options: It decreases until it becomes zero
questions.explanation: As speed increases, air resistance increases. The resultant force (Weight - Air Resistance) decreases. Since F = ma, acceleration decreases until it reaches zero at terminal velocity.

questions.question: A swimmer pushes water backwards to move forward. Which law explains this motion?
questions.explanation: The swimmer exerts a backward force on the water (action). The water exerts an equal and opposite forward force on the swimmer (reaction), propelling them forward.

questions.question: An object moves with constant velocity in a straight line. What can be said about the forces acting on it?
options: There are no forces acting on the object
The driving force is greater than friction
The object has no resistance to change
questions.explanation: According to Newton's First Law, if an object moves with constant velocity, the forces are balanced and the resultant (unbalanced) force is zero.

questions.question: A car of mass 1000 kg accelerates at 2 m/s². The total resistive force is 500 N. What is the engine force?
questions.explanation: Resultant force F = ma = 1000 kg × 2 m/s² = 2000 N. Engine Force = Resultant + Resistive = 2000 N + 500 N = 2500 N (Syllabus 3j).

questions.question: What happens to the air resistance acting on a skydiver immediately after opening their parachute?
questions.explanation: Opening the parachute greatly increases the surface area, causing air resistance (drag) to increase rapidly. This creates an upward resultant force, slowing the skydiver down.

questions.question: Why do action and reaction forces not cancel each other out?
options: They are not equal in magnitude
They are in the same direction
questions.explanation: Forces only cancel if they act on the same body. Action-reaction pairs act on different objects, so they produce effects on different objects and do not cancel (Syllabus 3g).

questions.question: Which velocity-time graph represents an object falling and reaching terminal velocity?
options: A straight line with constant positive gradient
A curve with decreasing gradient becoming horizontal
A horizontal line from the start
questions.explanation: Initially, acceleration (gradient) is high. As speed increases, air resistance increases, reducing acceleration. At terminal velocity, acceleration is zero, so the graph becomes horizontal (constant velocity).

questions.question: Object A has mass 2 kg and Object B has mass 10 kg. Which object has greater resistance to change in motion?
options: Resistance depends on speed, not mass
questions.explanation: Resistance to change in motion is directly proportional to mass. Object B has 5 times the mass of Object A, so it has 5 times the resistance to change.

questions.question: A book rests on a table. The weight of the book is the action force. What is the reaction force?
options: The normal force of the table on the book
The gravitational pull of the book on the Earth
The friction between the book and table
The air resistance on the book
questions.explanation: Action-reaction pairs act on different objects. Weight is Earth pulling Book. The reaction is Book pulling Earth (gravitational pull of the book on the Earth). The normal force is a separate contact force.

questions.question: A trolley is pulled by a constant force. If the mass of the trolley is doubled while the force remains constant, what happens to the acceleration?
questions.explanation: From F = ma, acceleration is inversely proportional to mass (a = F/m). If mass doubles, acceleration halves for the same unbalanced force.
